acceptance_criteria.given: A page that is shorter than the viewport height
acceptance_criteria.then: The 'back to top' control is not present in the DOM or is hidden from view.

acceptance_criteria.given: A page that is taller than the viewport height
acceptance_criteria.then: The 'back to top' control is not visible.
acceptance_criteria.when: The user has not yet scrolled

acceptance_criteria.given: A page that is taller than the viewport height
acceptance_criteria.then: The 'back to top' control becomes visible in the footer.
acceptance_criteria.when: The user scrolls down the page

acceptance_criteria.given: The 'back to top' control is visible
acceptance_criteria.then: The page performs a smooth scroll animation to the top (y=0).
acceptance_criteria.when: The user clicks the icon or presses Enter/Space while focused

acceptance_criteria.then: The device announces 'Back to top' (via aria-label).
acceptance_criteria.when: The user navigates to the control

acceptance_criteria.then: The build must pass with no linting errors or warnings.

assumptions.assumption: The 'smooth scroll' behavior is handled via CSS (scroll-behavior: smooth) or standard Web APIs.
The icon will be implemented as an SVG or an icon font already present in the project.

clarified_description: Add an icon-based 'back to top' control within the existing sandbox site footer. The control should only become visible once a user has begun scrolling on a page that is long enough to require scrolling. When activated, the control will perform a smooth scroll back to the top of the page. The control must be accessible via keyboard navigation and provide clear context to screen-reader users via an aria-label.

constraints.detail: Must pass all existing repository linting and CI checks.
Scroll event listeners must be optimized (e.g., debounced or using IntersectionObserver) to avoid main-thread jank.

must: The control must be an icon-based trigger (e.g., an upward arrow).
The control must be grouped with existing elements in the site footer.
The control must only be visible if the page is scrollable AND the user has initiated a scroll event.
The control must trigger a smooth scroll animation to the top of the document.
The control must be focusable via keyboard (Tab key).
The control must include an `aria-label="Back to top"` for screen-reader accessibility.
The implementation must pass all existing repository linting and build checks.
outcome: Users can return to the top of long pages with a single, smooth action via a footer-based icon.
rationale: The requirement for visibility only after scrolling prevents 'dead' UI elements on short pages. Using an icon in the footer maintains a clean aesthetic while the smooth scroll and aria-label ensure high usability and accessibility standards.

risks.mitigation: Ensure all code follows the project's established Prettier/ESLint configurations before submission.
risks.title: Linting failures

should: The icon should be visually consistent with the existing sandbox site design language.

jobs_to_be_done: Quickly navigate back to the top of a long content page.
users.name: General User
pain_points: Manual scrolling or repeated keyboard presses to reach the header.

jobs_to_be_done: Navigate the site structure using keyboard or screen reader.
users.name: Assistive Technology User
pain_points: Lack of clear semantic meaning for icon-only buttons.

wireframes.title: Sandbox Footer with Back to Top

wont: The control will not be a floating/fixed position element (it must reside in the footer).
The control will not appear as a text-only link.
